audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Business Analytics combines mathematics, statistics, programming and data science with business decisions. Students apply analytical methods in marketing, finance, accounting and operations, with responsible data use, recurring business-data projects and reporting. The final year includes study abroad, restricted disciplinary choices, a project or approved internship and an individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR option combines data analysis, mathematics and computing with economics, finance, accounting and marketing. Maastricht develops those subjects through a dedicated sequence of business-data projects, operations courses, reporting, study abroad and an individual thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The final year includes 26 EC of study abroad, one 6.5 EC choice from each of two disciplinary menus, a 13 EC project or regional internship and an 8 EC individual thesis.

componentNotes.y3-01: The standard programme requires study abroad. Maastricht’s regulations govern eligibility and exceptions.
componentNotes.y3-02: Choose one course from the period-four menu.
componentNotes.y3-03: Choose one course from the period-five menu.
componentNotes.y3-04: Choose the research project or an approved regional internship. Either carries 13 EC.
componentNotes.y3-05: An individually written academic paper worth 8 EC.

notes.text: UCR teaches R for data preparation and visualisation, Python programming, statistics, machine learning and business applications. Maastricht also requires dedicated R and web-development skills courses, two eLab business cases, operations and supply-chain analytics, specialised reporting, a 13 EC research project or regional internship, and an 8 EC individual thesis.

Maastricht’s final year includes 26 EC of study abroad, two restricted disciplinary choices worth 13 EC in total, a 13 EC project or regional internship and an 8 EC individual thesis. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the displayed 180 EC schedule.

ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

ENSSUST313.name: Research in a Sustainable Delta
ENSSUST313.text: In this project course you will work in small teams of two or three students on a research problem relevant for sustainability in the broadest sense. We are looking for collaborations with local companies and other institutions. The research questions are supplied by a regional institution or company that is active in areas related to sustainability in the broadest sense. In this way it is guaranteed that the research projects are indeed relevant for the Zeeland delta. Furthermore, students will have access to expertise and/or facilities of the external partner, which will broaden their perspective. Usually, there will be one person affiliated with the external partner organization involved with a project team as external advisor

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.text: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

Laboratory exercises and projects develop algorithm implementation, evaluation and experimental investigation of small intelligent systems.
